questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How lost cats and dogs find their way home
Why cats make better pets than dogs
How birds fly long distances
The world's biggest pets
questions.why: Dan says the topic is how cats and dogs find their way home over long distances.

questions.q: Why does Neil say he is a 'cat person'?
options: Cats are cleaner than dogs
He grew up with cats
Cats are better at finding their way home
He thinks dogs are hard work
questions.why: Neil says he's a cat person because dogs are 'hard work'.

questions.q: What did a cat called Holly do?
options: Became the world's longest cat
Helped scientists study magnets
Travelled about 200 miles to get home
Found a lost dog
questions.why: Neil says a lost cat called Holly travelled 200 miles to get home.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the ideas mentioned for how pets navigate?
options: A strong sense of smell
Following the position of the sun
Recognising landmarks
The Earth's magnetic force
questions.why: They mention smell, visual landmarks and magnetic forces, but not the sun.

questions.q: What is said about how birds navigate?
options: They follow smells carried on the wind from home
They use Earth's magnetism, maybe with iron in their beaks
They remember landmarks like mountains and rivers
They follow older birds that have made the trip before
questions.why: Neil says birds use the Earth's magnetic force, and they may have iron in their beaks.

questions.q: According to Dr John Bradshaw, how does a cat learn a new area?
options: It follows its owner around the garden for weeks
It stays close to the house for the first few months
It explores in bigger circles to make a map in its head
It walks in a straight line until it gets tired
questions.why: He says cats go out in 'ever-increasing circles' and construct a mental map.

questions.q: What does Dr Bradshaw think a lost cat does?
options: Searches in growing circles for a familiar place or smell
Waits in one place until its owner comes to find it
Asks other cats in the area for help finding home
Uses the sun and the stars to find the way north
questions.why: He says it goes out in growing circles until it finds its territory or a smell from it on the wind.

questions.q: How certain is Dr Bradshaw about his explanation?
options: Completely sure, because it's been proved
He thinks it's wrong
He says only dogs behave this way
It's a theory, as there still isn't enough data
questions.why: Dan says it's the theory, but Dr Bradshaw says we still don't have enough data.
